title: The Dental Misinformation Epidemic: An Evaluation of Quality, Accuracy and Educational Impact in Youtube's Tooth Bleaching Content
screen_reason: QUALITY-ONLY study (INSTRUCTIONS §1 exclusion, §3 definition). Despite the title's 'misinformation epidemic' framing, the 43 Portuguese-language tooth-bleaching videos are never judged true or false against any external ground truth. Every reported share is a score distribution on a quality/reliability instrument: modified DISCERN reliability (1-5), the Global Quality Score (1-5), a five-item usefulness checklist (0-5, one point per key aspect 'accurately addressed'), and a good/moderate/poor audiovisual-production rating. A fully accurate video can score low on all four (e.g. by not citing sources, or by not covering all five usefulness items), which is exactly the case §3 assigns to QUALITY. No share of videos coded false, misleading or inaccurate is reported anywhere, so the paper yields no CONTENT prevalence estimate.
missed_or_uncertain: Candidate QUALITY figures, recorded here for the adjudicator in case the project's convention is to keep a QUALITY row (§3 'row kept, excluded from prevalence') rather than exclude the paper at screening. Denominator throughout: 43 Portuguese-language YouTube videos on tooth bleaching (Brazil, Google Trends terms, searched December 2024; 366 retrieved, 3 over 60 min, 284 under 1 min and 36 off-topic excluded); two independent raters, Cohen's kappa 0.92 (95% CI 0.89-0.94). (a) modified DISCERN reliability <=2: abstract and Discussion say '71.4% of videos demonstrated low reliability (scores <= 2/5)', but Section 3.4 says 'The cumulative analysis indicates that 44.2% of all videos scored <= 2' and Table 3's own cells sum to 19/43 = 44.2% (1: 4; 2: 15) - the paper contradicts itself and 71.4% cannot be reproduced from any table, so no value is safely keepable under R8. (b) GQS <=2: '44.2% of all videos scored <= 2 on the quality scale' (Section 3.3), consistent with Table 2 (score 1: 16 videos = 37.2%; score 2: 3 = 7.0%). (c) 'only 4.7% achieved maximum quality (5/5 GQS)' in the abstract conflicts with Table 2, where 5/43 = 11.6% score 5 on quality and 4.7% (n=2) is the top RELIABILITY cell; the Discussion mixes the two ('only 4.7% (n = 2) of videos achieved maximum reliability scores and 11.6% (n = 5) demonstrated excellent overall quality'). (d) usefulness score 0: 18/43 videos (30.2% 'Bleaching Teeth' + 11.6% 'Bleaching Toothpaste'), a cross-category sum I did not keep. (e) '57.7% of dentist-published videos failing to meet basic usefulness standards (scores <= 2)' is a source subgroup on a usefulness scale, and its denominator (number of dentist-published videos) is never given. (f) '100% of videos rated as having high/moderate technical standards' is production quality, not veracity. (g) 'A comprehensive analysis of 50 charcoal-based bleaching toothpastes ... revealed that merely 8% contained fluoride' is a figure the paper cites from reference 25, excluded by R8, and is a product-composition share, not a misinformation share. Note also that the three search terms named in Methods ('Clareamento dental', 'Clarear dentes', 'Creme dental clareador') are relabelled in the Results and tables as 'types of tooth bleaching', 'whitening toothpaste' and 'how to bleach teeth', and the per-term counts (15 + 15 + 13 = 43) are stated inconsistently with Table 1's category labels.

rob.design: Cross-sectional infodemiology study of YouTube; three search terms chosen from Google Trends (Brazil, last 12 months, Health category, YouTube), searched December 2024; 366 videos retrieved, 43 included after excluding >60 min (n=3), <1 min (n=284) and off-topic (n=36); two independent researchers (LALS, HJSR) rated every video on modified DISCERN reliability, GQS overall quality, a five-item usefulness checklist and a three-level audiovisual-quality rating; inter-rater agreement reported as Cohen's kappa = 0.92 (95% CI 0.89-0.94) for the assessment criteria as a whole (no per-instrument kappa); descriptive statistics only (Jamovi 2.3.28); no veracity/fact-check coding, no external ground truth, and several internally inconsistent percentages between abstract, text and tables (44.2% vs 71.4% low reliability; 4.7% vs 11.6% top score).
rob.item6_quote: The reliability of the videos was assessed using the modified DISCERN scale [19], which evaluates a material's ability to present consistent results while minimizing discrepancies with potential sources. This scale consists of five key criteria: (1) clarity of objectives, (2) use of reliable information sources, (3) impartiality, (4) inclusion of additional reference sources, and (5) acknowledgment of areas of uncertainty regarding the subject matter.
rob.item10_quote: The cumulative percentage analysis indicates that 44.2% of all videos scored ≤ 2 on the quality scale, suggesting substantial room for improvement in overall content quality.
